subject: chemistry
question_text: State the first law of thermodynamics.

verification.note: PREDICTED, not asked. This question comes from the enumeration sweep of the Thermodynamics syllabus: the Fastrack chemistry section (book pp.73-75) asks the second law (VSAQ 6), the third law (VSAQ 7) and the mathematical form of the first law as an SAQ, but never the plain two-mark statement of the first law itself. Only ONE source book is held for chemistry, so the two-book union check is PENDING — a second source may show this asked. This chapter has NO Long Answer section in the book, so no 8-mark form is invented. The 1+1 mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Sign convention: ΔU = q + w with w = work done ON the system (NCERT), matching the SAQ card ts_ipe_c1_td_first_law_math.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The statement
lines: First law of thermodynamics: energy can
neither be created nor destroyed; it can
only change from one form to another.
The total energy of the universe is
steps.why: The first law is the law of conservation of energy applied to heat and work — it counts every joule a system gains or loses.
common_mistakes: Mixing in entropy — that is the second law, not the first.
steps.memory_tip: First law: energy is conserved. Second law: entropy increases. Keep the two sentences apart.
steps.margin_note: The conservation sentence earns this mark.

steps.label: Mathematical form
lines: For a system absorbing heat q, with w the

lines.text: ΔU = q + w (w = work done on the system)

steps.why: The equation is the law in symbols: the internal energy changes only by the heat and the work that cross the boundary. With w counted as work done on the system, both terms enter with plus signs.
common_mistakes: Writing ΔU = q − w while calling w the work done on the system — the minus form belongs to the older work-done-by convention.
steps.memory_tip: Both q and w are energy given to the system, so both are added.
steps.margin_note: State whose work w is; the sign convention is part of the equation.

insider_note: Two marks, and the second is the equation with its sign convention named. ΔU = q + w is only correct when w is stated as the work done on the system; without that sentence the equation is ambiguous.
